deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can destroy the resource on 'destroy'/'apply'. Setting to 'PREVENT' guards against accidental route deletion; policy should whitelist 'PREVENT' for production routes.

description.description: A free-text description of the resource. Max length 1024 characters.
description.rationale: Free-text field with no functional or access-control impact; purely descriptive metadata.

gateways.description:
Gateways defines a list of gateways this HttpRoute is attached to, as one of the routing rules to route the requests served by the gateway.
Each gateway reference should match the pattern: projects/*/locations/global/gateways/<gateway_name>
gateways.rationale: Controls which Gateway resources this route is attached to; attaching to an unapproved or overly permissive gateway can expose routing to unintended external traffic.

hostnames.description: Set of hosts that should match against the HTTP host header to select a HttpRoute to process the request.
hostnames.rationale: Determines which HTTP Host headers this route matches. An overly broad or wildcard hostname can cause traffic to be routed unexpectedly, a common source of misrouting and security exposure.

labels.description:
Set of label tags associated with the HttpRoute resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels support governance controls like environment classification, cost tracking, and label-based compliance automation. Policy should require a baseline set of mandatory keys (e.g. environment, owner).

meshes.description:
Meshes defines a list of meshes this HttpRoute is attached to, as one of the routing rules to route the requests served by the mesh.
Each mesh reference should match the pattern: projects/*/locations/global/meshes/<mesh_name>.
The attached Mesh should be of a type SIDECAR.
meshes.rationale: Controls which service mesh resources this route is attached to; an unapproved or overly permissive mesh binding can expose internal service traffic incorrectly.

name.rationale: Resource identifier only; naming has no functional security impact beyond optional org naming conventions.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Determines which GCP project the resource is created in; an unpinned or incorrect project can place resources outside intended security boundaries or monitoring scope.

rules.description: Rules that define how traffic is routed and handled.

rules.action.description: The detailed rule defining how to route matched traffic.

rules.action.timeout.description: Specifies the timeout for selected route.
rules.action.timeout.rationale: Controls request timeout behavior only; a purely operational reliability tuning parameter with no access-control or data-exposure implications, consistent with per_try_timeout.

rules.action.cors_policy.description: The specification for allowing client side cross-origin requests.

rules.action.cors_policy.allow_credentia.description: In response to a preflight request, setting this to true indicates that the actual request can include user credentials.
rules.action.cors_policy.allow_credentia.rationale: Allowing credentials on CORS responses expands the attack surface for cross-origin credential theft; this setting should be paired with a tightly scoped allow_origins/allow_origin_regexes list, never a wildcard origin, and its use should be reviewed.

rules.action.cors_policy.allow_headers.description: Specifies the content for Access-Control-Allow-Headers header.

rules.action.cors_policy.allow_methods.description: Specifies the content for Access-Control-Allow-Methods header.

rules.action.cors_policy.allow_origin_re.description: Specifies the regular expression patterns that match allowed origins.

rules.action.cors_policy.allow_origins.description: Specifies the list of origins that will be allowed to do CORS requests.
rules.action.cors_policy.allow_origins.rationale: A wildcard ('*') in allow_origins permits any website to make cross-origin requests to this route. Combined with credentialed requests this is a well-known CORS misconfiguration that can expose the service to cross-origin data theft. Policy should blacklist the wildcard and require an explicit, approved origin list.

rules.action.cors_policy.disabled.description: If true, the CORS policy is disabled. The default value is false, which indicates that the CORS policy is in effect.
rules.action.cors_policy.disabled.rationale: Disabling the CORS policy entirely removes origin and credential restrictions that may be relied upon for security, effectively allowing unrestricted cross-origin access to this route.

rules.action.cors_policy.expose_headers.description: Specifies the content for Access-Control-Expose-Headers header.

rules.action.cors_policy.max_age.description: Specifies how long result of a preflight request can be cached in seconds.

rules.action.destinations.description: The destination to which traffic should be forwarded.

rules.action.destinations.service_name.description: The URL of a BackendService to route traffic to.

rules.action.destinations.weight.description:
Specifies the proportion of requests forwarded to the backend referenced by the serviceName field. This is computed as: weight/Sum(weights in this destination list). For non-zero values, there may be some epsilon from the exact proportion defined here depending on the precision an implementation supports.
If only one serviceName is specified and it has a weight greater than 0, 100% of the traffic is forwarded to that backend.
If weights are specified for any one service name, they need to be specified for all of them.
If weights are unspecified for all services, then, traffic is distributed in equal proportions to all of them.

rules.action.fault_injection_policy.description: The specification for fault injection introduced into traffic to test the resiliency of clients to backend service failure.

rules.action.fault_injection_policy.abor.description: Specification of how client requests are aborted as part of fault injection before being sent to a destination.
The HTTP status code used to abort the request.
The percentage of traffic which will be aborted.
rules.action.fault_injection_policy.abor.rationale: Setting the abort percentage to 100 causes all matched traffic to fail, functioning as a complete self-inflicted denial of service if applied in production; values should be scoped and time-bound to controlled testing.

rules.action.fault_injection_policy.dela.description: Specification of how client requests are delayed as part of fault injection before being sent to a destination.
Specify a fixed delay before forwarding the request.
The percentage of traffic on which delay will be injected.

rules.action.redirect.description: If set, the request is directed as configured by this field.

rules.action.redirect.host_redirect.description: The host that will be used in the redirect response instead of the one that was supplied in the request.

rules.action.redirect.https_redirect.description: If set to true, the URL scheme in the redirected request is set to https.
rules.action.redirect.https_redirect.rationale: Enforcing HTTPS on redirected requests prevents traffic from being downgraded to unencrypted HTTP, protecting against interception and downgrade attacks.

rules.action.redirect.path_redirect.description: The path that will be used in the redirect response instead of the one that was supplied in the request. pathRedirect can not be supplied together with prefixRedirect. Supply one alone or neither. If neither is supplied, the path of the original request will be used for the redirect.

rules.action.redirect.port_redirect.description: The port that will be used in the redirected request instead of the one that was supplied in the request.

rules.action.redirect.prefix_rewrite.description: Indicates that during redirection, the matched prefix (or path) should be swapped with this value.

rules.action.redirect.response_code.description: The HTTP Status code to use for the redirect.
rules.action.redirect.response_code.rationale: The correct redirect status code depends entirely on the intended semantics of the specific redirect (method/body preservation vs. permanence); there is no universally unsafe value, so this is not something a standalone policy can meaningfully enforce.

rules.action.redirect.strip_query.description: If set to true, any accompanying query portion of the original URL is removed prior to redirecting the request.
rules.action.redirect.strip_query.rationale: Whether preserving the query string on redirect is risky depends entirely on what a specific route's query parameters contain; the default (preserving) exists for legitimate functional reasons (analytics, pagination state), so this is not something a standalone policy can meaningfully enforce without false positives.

rules.action.request_header_modifier.description: The specification for modifying the headers of a matching request prior to delivery of the request to the destination.

rules.action.request_header_modifier.add.description: Add the headers with given map where key is the name of the header, value is the value of the header.
rules.action.request_header_modifier.add.rationale: Allowing arbitrary header injection (e.g. spoofing trust headers like Authorization, X-Forwarded-For, or Cookie) is security-relevant, but the current policy engine has no mechanism to check for forbidden keys within a map(string) field - only fixed, known keys (as used in labels.rego) or list/scalar membership are supported. Flagging for reviewer: this needs new shared-helper logic to enforce, out of scope for a single-field policy.

rules.action.request_header_modifier.rem.description: Remove headers (matching by header names) specified in the list.
rules.action.request_header_modifier.rem.rationale: Removing headers before forwarding to the backend more commonly causes functional failures (e.g. stripped auth headers being rejected by the backend) than security exposure; there is no clear set of forbidden values to enforce here.

rules.action.request_header_modifier.set.description: Completely overwrite/replace the headers with given map where key is the name of the header, value is the value of the header.

rules.action.request_mirror_policy.description: Specifies the policy on how requests intended for the routes destination are shadowed to a separate mirrored destination.

rules.action.request_mirror_policy.desti.description: The destination the requests will be mirrored to.
The URL of a BackendService to route traffic to.

Specifies the proportion of requests forwarded to the backend referenced by the serviceName field. This is computed as: weight/Sum(weights in this destination list). For non-zero values, there may be some epsilon from the exact proportion defined here depending on the precision an implementation supports.
If only one serviceName is specified and it has a weight greater than 0, 100% of the traffic is forwarded to that backend.
If weights are specified for any one service name, they need to be specified for all of them.
If weights are unspecified for all services, then, traffic is distributed in equal proportions to all of them.
rules.action.request_mirror_policy.desti.rationale: Determines the proportion of traffic mirrored, not whether mirroring occurs or where; purely a load-distribution configuration value with no inherent safe/unsafe threshold, consistent with destinations.weight.

rules.action.response_header_modifier.description: The specification for modifying the headers of a response prior to sending the response back to the client.

rules.action.response_header_modifier.ad.description: Add the headers with given map where key is the name of the header, value is the value of the header.

rules.action.response_header_modifier.re.description: Remove headers (matching by header names) specified in the list.
rules.action.response_header_modifier.re.rationale: Removing browser-security response headers (e.g. Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options) before they reach the client strips real defenses against XSS, clickjacking, and downgrade attacks.

rules.action.response_header_modifier.se.description: Completely overwrite/replace the headers with given map where key is the name of the header, value is the value of the header.

rules.action.retry_policy.description: Specifies the retry policy associated with this route.

rules.action.retry_policy.num_retries.description: Specifies the allowed number of retries.
rules.action.retry_policy.num_retries.rationale: An excessive retry count can amplify load against a struggling backend during outages (a self-inflicted retry-storm/DoS pattern). Policy should cap num_retries to a safe upper bound.

rules.action.retry_policy.per_try_timeou.description: Specifies a non-zero timeout per retry attempt. A duration in seconds with up to nine fractional digits, ending with 's'. Example: "3.5s".
rules.action.retry_policy.per_try_timeou.rationale: Controls retry timing/latency behavior only; a purely operational reliability tuning parameter with no access-control or data-exposure implications.

rules.action.retry_policy.retry_conditio.description: Specifies one or more conditions when this retry policy applies.
rules.action.retry_policy.retry_conditio.rationale: Specifies which response conditions trigger a retry (e.g. 5xx, deadline-exceeded); operational resiliency configuration with no direct security control.

rules.action.url_rewrite.description: The specification for rewrite URL before forwarding requests to the destination.

rules.action.url_rewrite.host_rewrite.description: Prior to forwarding the request to the selected destination, the requests host header is replaced by this value.
rules.action.url_rewrite.host_rewrite.rationale: Rewriting the Host header sent to the backend can enable host-header-confusion or SSRF-adjacent misconfigurations if set to an untrusted or overly permissive value, so its use should be reviewed and constrained.

rules.action.url_rewrite.path_prefix_rew.description: Prior to forwarding the request to the selected destination, the matching portion of the requests path is replaced by this value.
rules.action.url_rewrite.path_prefix_rew.rationale: Rewriting the request path before forwarding to the backend can be misused to bypass path-based access controls or route requests to unintended internal endpoints if set to an untrusted or overly permissive value.

rules.matches.description:
A list of matches define conditions used for matching the rule against incoming HTTP requests. Each match is independent, i.e. this rule will be matched if ANY one of the matches is satisfied.
If no matches field is specified, this rule will unconditionally match traffic.
If a default rule is desired to be configured, add a rule with no matches specified to the end of the rules list.

rules.matches.full_path_match.description: The HTTP request path value should exactly match this value.

rules.matches.ignore_case.description: Specifies if prefixMatch and fullPathMatch matches are case sensitive. The default value is false.
rules.matches.ignore_case.rationale: Enabling case-insensitive path matching can allow requests to bypass rules that rely on exact-case path segments (e.g. a rule targeting '/Admin' could be matched by '/admin'), weakening path-based access controls.

rules.matches.prefix_match.description: The HTTP request path value must begin with specified prefixMatch. prefixMatch must begin with a /.

rules.matches.regex_match.description: The HTTP request path value must satisfy the regular expression specified by regexMatch after removing any query parameters and anchor supplied with the original URL. For regular expression grammar, please see https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax

rules.matches.headers.description: Specifies a list of HTTP request headers to match against.

rules.matches.headers.exact_match.description: The value of the header should match exactly the content of exactMatch.

rules.matches.headers.header.description: The name of the HTTP header to match against.

rules.matches.headers.invert_match.description: If specified, the match result will be inverted before checking. Default value is set to false.
rules.matches.headers.invert_match.rationale: This flag inverts the match result but carries no inherent security direction on its own; its impact is entirely contextual to the specific header match it modifies and is not something a standalone policy can meaningfully enforce.

rules.matches.headers.prefix_match.description: The value of the header must start with the contents of prefixMatch.

rules.matches.headers.present_match.description: A header with headerName must exist. The match takes place whether or not the header has a value.

rules.matches.headers.regex_match.description: The value of the header must match the regular expression specified in regexMatch.

rules.matches.headers.suffix_match.description: The value of the header must end with the contents of suffixMatch.

rules.matches.headers.range_match.description: If specified, the rule will match if the request header value is within the range.

rules.matches.query_parameters.description: Specifies a list of query parameters to match against.

rules.matches.query_parameters.exact_mat.description: The value of the query parameter must exactly match the contents of exactMatch.

rules.matches.query_parameters.present_m.description: Specifies that the QueryParameterMatcher matches if request contains query parameter, irrespective of whether the parameter has a value or not.

rules.matches.query_parameters.query_par.description: The name of the query parameter to match.

rules.matches.query_parameters.regex_mat.description: The value of the query parameter must match the regular expression specified by regexMatch.For regular expression grammar, please see https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax
